starting_principles: Parametric equations of projectile motion x(t) = (u cos theta) t and y(t) = (u sin theta) t - 0.5 g t^2

ordered_steps.action_description: Express time t as a function of horizontal position x from uniform horizontal motion
ordered_steps.justification: Constant horizontal velocity component u_x = u cos(theta).

ordered_steps.action_description: Substitute t into the vertical displacement equation
ordered_steps.justification: Elimination of parameter t to find spatial locus y(x).

ordered_steps.action_description: Simplify trigonometric terms using tan(theta) = sin(theta)/cos(theta)
ordered_steps.justification: Standard form of projectile trajectory parabola.

ordered_steps.action_description: Factor out x tan(theta) to express in terms of horizontal range R = u^2 sin(2 theta)/g
ordered_steps.equation_latex: y = x \tan\theta \left( 1 - \frac{g x}{2 u^2 \cos^2\theta \tan\theta} \right) = x \tan\theta \left( 1 - \frac{g x}{2 u^2 \sin\theta \cos\theta} \right) = x \tan\theta \left( 1 - \frac{x}{R} \right)
ordered_steps.justification: Using double-angle identity sin(2 theta) = 2 sin(theta) cos(theta).

applicability_conditions: Valid for projectile launched from origin (0, 0)
source_references: Concepts of Physics Vol 1 by H.C. Verma (Chapter 3, pp. 54-55)
